The Battle of Indus River in 1027 AD refers to a naval expedition by Mahmud of Ghazni against the jats of Multan. The battle ended with the victory of mahmud over the jats on the Indus River.
Battle
Mahmud was going back to Ghazna after the expedition against the hindus in the Somnath, But some jats looted his comrades and harassed them in the way. Mahmud retaliated in 1027 AD against jats.
Mahmud arrived in Multan and constructed the small fleets of 1,400 boats. In each boat, mahmud stationed 20 men consists of bows, arrows and naphtha. On the other hand, jats collected 4,000 to 8,000 boats. Mahmud's superior boats and used of naphtha fire give upper hand to him and he defeated the jats in the naval battle. Many jats were killed in the battle and their family members take prisoners.
